Information has become a huge topic in today's world, and the value of such information is at an all time high. Every conceivable way your information is subject to the will of others. If you don't protect yourself, and your information, it WILL be exploited. Over the years, it's become clear to me that there is an overwhelming amount of people who simply don't know how to protect themselves and regain some of their privacy. This thread has been a long time coming, and I hope it will serve everyone well as a fairly large and complete trove of information on how to stay private, and also gain some security and anonyminity.

I will break this down into sections, and will have comments below that will serve as sections for each section above for everyone to leave their own suggestions and comments on each section.

How to stay safe on your computer:

Operating System:

I know this gets mentioned all the time, but not using Windows is a huge head start into regaining your privacy. Switch to Linux. There are unlimited resources available to you for this endeavor: /v/linux is a great start. Try the different subs aimed at your particular distribution.

Some available distributions (in no particular order, and without bias) include:

  • Linux Mint
  • Ubuntu
  • ElementaryOS
  • Debian
  • Fedora

You can also visit their respective subs for more information:

  • /v/linuxmint
  • /v/ubuntu
  • /v/elementaryos
  • /v/debian
  • /v/fedora

Browsers:

To obtain a higher level of privacy, consider changing your browser. Firefox is known to be the most private browser. Chrome is the worst when it comes to privacy. This should be fairly obvious since Google makes Chrome, and Google is one of the largets privacy offenders.

Some available browsers (in no particular order, and without bias) include:

  • Firefox
  • Iridium Browser
  • Pale Moon

You can also visit their respective subs for more information:

  • /v/firefox

Browsers also have add-ons and extentions that can greatly change the functionality of the browser. Some of the best suggestions are below. Keep in mind, not all add-ons have versions for different browsers. There may be an add-on for one browser that's not available for another, but there might be another add-on for that browser under a different name.

Some available add-ons (in no particular order, and without bias) include:

  • HTTPS:// EVERYWHERE
  • Privacy Badger
  • uBlock Origin - For Firefox based browsers
  • uBlock Origin - For Chromium based browsers
  • NoScript - Probably the best protection you can get in a browser. (Firefox Only)
  • No Resource URI Leak (Firefox Only)

Search Engines:

Search engines can be a huge privacy nightmare. If you are using one of the big names, like Google, Bing, or Yahoo, expect to have zero privacy with regard to your searches, and web history. There are plenty of great search engines that respect your privacy.

Some available search engines (in no particular order, and without bias) include:

  • Duck Duck Go
  • Startpage
  • ixquick
  • Disconnect
  • Searx

Email:

There are plenty of email providers that will respect your privacy. Some do charge a nominal fee, but others are free, and offer top notch privacy and security. As always, if you are using any of the big name providers such as Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, ect, expect to have zero privacy with respect to your email and contacts.

Some available email providers (in no particular order, and without bias) include:

  • Tutanota
  • Mailbox.org
  • ProtonMail

Anonymizing Networks:

There are a couple of anonymizing networks available to you. Keep in mind, these are pieces of software you should take the time to understand a bit if you plan on using them.

  • Tor
  • i2p

Other Software Alternatives (in no particular order, and without bias) include::

  • Skype Alternative - Wire

Other:

There are a lot of other ways to maintain privacy on your computer, involving various configuration and habit changes. A few suggestions are as follows:

  • Use a custom HOSTS file - For further reading on this, see Wikipedia entry on HOSTS files and a very popular HOSTS file
  • Use Private Mode, or Incognito Mode in your browser.
  • Consider using a VPN. This will likely cost money and you will need to research a provider.
  • Consider Whole Disk Encryption. This will encrypt your hard drive completely. It will not be able to boot until you enter the key when you first turn it on. You should take the time to understand this subbject a bit if you plan on implementing disk encryption of any kind.
  • Consider closing accounts you have with Facebook, Google, Microsoft, Yahoo, and many more of the big name web companies. They are almost exclusively making money by selling everything they can find out about you.
  • Keep a separate email account for junk mail and registrations. This will drastically reduce the exposure your real information has.

Phones:

If you have a smartphone, you have a humongous privacy issue. Unfortunately, fixing this to the point you regain some privacy may be too technical for some people. The good news is you can almost always easily find someone who can assist with this. This section will be a breif overview to prevent people from damaging their devices. This is just merely suggestions on what to do IF you can do it yourself, or know someone who can assist. These suggestions will almost always void your warranty as well. Most of the suggestions from the "Computer" section above will apply here with some differences.

  • If rooted, install AdAway
  • Install Silence or Signal as a replacement text messaging app
  • Avoid reinstalling Google Play or any other Google apps and services. Use F-Droid instead
  • Install Replicant

Non-Technology related privacy suggestions:

There are also other things you can do outside of your digital life that will help limit the exposure of your information. As always, educate yourself on what these are:

  • Opt-Out Pre-Screen will limit the sharing of your information for pre-qualified credit offers and offers of insurance. Great for reducing junk mail!
  • DMA Choice will limit the sharing of your information for all sorts of marketing databases. Also great for reducing junk mail!
  • If you do a change of address with the USPS - they will sell your information

This is not meant to be an exhaustive resource on privacy, but rather, a head start for those who do not know where to start. Feel free to check out these resources for more information:

  • PrivacyTools.io
  • Prism-Break.org
